A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TetSphere Splatting work. Their complete main texts, appendices, figures, tables and equations support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original GSO reconstruction results, generated shapes, computational measurements and dense-view inverse-rendering experiments, including Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains original reconstruction and generation results and adds multi-view quantitative evaluations in Tables 1 and 4 and qualitative comparisons in Figure 5.

M1.justification: The tetrahedral-sphere representation, silhouette-coverage initialization, deformation objective, bi-harmonic regularization, non-inversion penalty and texture/PBR procedures remain the same. Testing the existing framework with depth supervision does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: v1 already includes dense-view GSO reconstruction in Appendix B. v3 replaces that study with broader multi-view coverage involving closed and open surfaces from Thingi32, DeepFashion3D, Objaverse and Adobe Stock. The GSO sorter appeared previously in v1 Figure 12; the 30-object GSO single-view evaluation remains.

E2.justification: v3 adds multi-view comparisons against NIE, FlexiCubes, 2DGS and DMesh, while dropping the earlier comparison against Nicolet et al. (2021). The single-view table removes RealFusion, Point-E, Shap-E and Zero123. Magic123, DreamCraft3D and RichDreamer remain in their generation comparisons.

E3.justification: The new multi-view evaluation uses rendered RGBA/depth inputs and mask/depth losses, adding F-Score, Normal Consistency, Edge Chamfer and Edge F-Score metrics. For single-view reconstruction, v3's six Wonder3D views agree with v1 Appendix A and resolve v1 Section 6.2's contradictory eight-view statement; this does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The coefficient, normal-loss and non-inversion ablations are retained unchanged from v1 Figure 8 to v3 Figure 6. v3 adds a limited qualitative failure analysis of thin plant leaves against DMesh. The dedicated convergence and topology case discussion against Nicolet et al. in v1 Appendix B is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added result tables continue reporting single summary values.

E6.justification: Retained single-view scores and SDS speed/memory measurements are unchanged. New multi-view results include TetSphere ALR 0.6602 and IoU 0.6844; DMesh has lower Chamfer distance, 0.0136 versus 0.0184, and FlexiCubes has lower runtime, 57.67 versus 934 seconds. Removed baseline rows and dense-view comparisons eliminate earlier results. Text-generation examples expand, while the mushroom/teddy image-generation comparison disappears.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 retain the same constrained and penalized objectives, deformation-gradient derivation and initialization formulation. The paracompactness argument is retained. No substantive mathematical definition, theorem or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: v3 drops the abstract's broad optimization-speed superiority claim and centers the contribution on mesh quality with competitive reconstruction accuracy. Generation becomes supporting demonstration and texture optimization is explicitly secondary. The principal representation and mesh-quality contributions remain.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly acknowledges weaker thin-shell modeling, with DMesh more accurate on plant leaves, qualifying the earlier emphasis on thin-structure robustness. Computational advantages are discussed separately for multi-view reconstruction and SDS generation. The limitation concerning topology preservation across sphere unions remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Most implementation information is retained or relocated, including C++/Gurobi, CUDA/PyTorch and generation texture settings. v3 documents inputs and losses for its new multi-view evaluation, but removes the earlier dense-view Mitsuba setup, 3,000/10,000-iteration budgets and Nicolet comparator hyperparameters.

R1.justification: The introduction substantially repositions TetSphere around mesh-quality limitations of contemporary Lagrangian primitives, beyond the earlier emphasis on Eulerian computational costs. Added research includes DMesh, 2DGS, SuGaR, MeshAnything, NIE, FlexiCubes and newer reconstruction models; older template-based reconstruction discussion is shortened.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten. The separate Overview section is absorbed into the method presentation, initialization and texture discussion are consolidated, experiments are reorganized around reconstruction, and implementation and supplementary sections are redistributed. These changes substantially alter the narrative structure.

P2.justification: v3 redraws the pipeline and introductory comparison figures, removes the initialization diagram, adds multi-view displays and expands the text-generation montage. Retained tables replace mesher-specific categories with Eulerian/Lagrangian groupings. Several generation figures move into the appendix, alongside extensive typography and page-layout changes.

improvement.justification: v1's quantitative reconstruction evidence centers on diffusion-assisted single-view GSO results, with qualitative multi-view evidence against one surface-mesh comparator. v3 substantially strengthens validation through direct multi-view comparisons against several Eulerian and Lagrangian methods, additional accuracy and edge metrics, and an explicit thin-shell failure case. These gains improve support and qualification of the central geometry claim, despite removing several earlier comparisons and their implementation details.
